episodes.title: AI:AM: Is THIS the AI We Want? Alarming Acceleration, AI Election Bets, GPU Trading & AI-Native VC
episodes.about: Nathan Labenz and Prakash Narayanan examine mounting evidence of rapid AI acceleration alongside guests Brian Zhou of Thoughtful, Mike San Miguel of Luxor Technology, and Bryan Bischof of Theory Ventures. The discussions unpack how frontier agents fared when trading real money on midterm election forecasts, the intense physical constraints and compliance rules shaping secondary GPU transactions, and how venture firms use thousands of agent runs to identify alpha. Anchored by METR's assessment and Anthropic's amended regulatory filings, the hosts explore whether frontier labs are on the brink of dramatic, AI-driven progress that could outpace human oversight.
episodes.why: Out yesterday: agents put real money on midterm forecasts, GPUs trade under compliance rules, and METR's acceleration numbers anchor a direct argument about whether oversight can keep up.

episodes.title: METR Inside Anthropic: 12x Gains From Unreleased Models
episodes.about: METR's report from inside Anthropic finds unreleased models helping build the next generation and employees self-reporting 12x productivity gains: four internal-only models, internal models now used to build the next ones, roughly two years of progress in one year, and no obvious bottleneck. The episode also covers Perplexity putting Teammates on its $200 Max plan, an experiment where editing 0.016% of Qwen 3.5's weights lifted its math score from 7.2% to 42%, and the market sell-off tied to data-center resistance after the election.
episodes.why: METR got inside Anthropic and found four unreleased models already building their successors, with staff reporting 12x gains - the clearest recursive-improvement data point yet published.

episodes.title: Facial recognition can find missing people. It can find you, too.
episodes.about: A missing daughter. An unidentified body. A single photograph. Facial recognition technology is helping police solve cases that once seemed impossible. But the same technology can identify just about anyone. In this CyberMonday crossover with WAMU and NPR's 1A, we revisit a story about the surprising power of facial recognition, then talk with Clare Garvie of the NYU Policing Project about what happens when your face no longer belongs just to you.
episodes.why: One photograph is now enough for police to name a missing person or an unidentified body; Clare Garvie walks through what that same capability means for everyone else's face.

episodes.title: The hidden supply chain costs of the AI boom
episodes.about: Nilay Patel talks with Willy Shih, a Harvard Business School professor of management practice and author of the upcoming book Where Does My Stuff Come From?, about the economics underneath global supply chains: Trump's tariffs, why markets have reacted to supply-chain disruptions the way they have, the global memory shortage pushing RAM prices up, and why China remains a manufacturing powerhouse even though every other country thinks that's so risky.
episodes.why: The AI boom runs on memory chips and factories, not just models: Shih explains the RAM shortage and the China dependence the buildout cannot route around.

episodes.title: The AI Agent Race: Perplexity Teammates, Meta Muse & GPT-6 Cyber
episodes.about: AI is moving beyond answers and into getting things done. Jaeden Schafer breaks down the latest wave of AI agents, including Perplexity Teammates, Meta Muse's voice and avatar features, and Airbnb's plans for an AI travel assistant. The roundup also covers OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber, Thinking Machines' Inkling model, Google's video-generation updates, and Anthropic's work on protein research, and asks what makes an agent genuinely useful - and which tools are worth paying for.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — AI Breakdown is Jaeden Schafer's short daily AI news roundup, new here: 15 minutes on this week's agent launches, from Perplexity Teammates to OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber.
